problem:
Given the **orthonormal** basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}$, where ${x}_{3}$ is the third component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]},\,x=[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2},\,{q}_{3}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=x\cdot {q}_{i}.$ Computing ${x}_{3},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} & =x\cdot {q}_{3} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{2} \\ -\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\sqrt{5}+0+0 \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
-\frac{1}{2}{x}_{3}=-\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{5}=-\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}.
$$
